# vela3-mini

Vela 3.0 on d3-mini: more accuracy than vela3-lite, with the built-in questions still on trained adapters and spans.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Repository | [`vllm-sr/vela3-mini`](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/vela3-mini), pinned at `bbc0206efbbb` |
| Family | [Vela 3.0](model-runtime/supported-models/vela-3/overview.md) |
| Parameters | 4.79B loaded |
| Backbone | Qwen3.5 text |
| Base package | [`vllm-sr/d3-mini`](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/d3-mini) at `566da0ea398e` |
| Precision (`--dtype auto`) | BF16 on a GPU, FP32 on a CPU |
| Weights | about 9.6 GB at BF16, 19.2 GB at FP32 |
| Device memory | 16 GiB or more |
| Reads | text, image, video |

## Question types

| Type | Answers |
| --- | --- |
| `choice` | Yes |
| `noul` | Yes |
| `score` | Yes |
| `set` | Yes, asked as one `noul` per label |
| `span` | Yes, on the `router` span head |

Rules that read the turn's images (`input.image`) or videos (`input.video`) can
resolve to it.

## Built-in questions

The Vela 3.0 family was trained on the Router's built-in
questions, so the Router asks each one in its trained form; the
[support matrix](system-one/reference/support-matrix.md) lists which.

:::note
This model has no calibrated thresholds: a built-in question without a
`predicate` uses 0.5, and the configuration load warns with
`uncalibrated_preset`.
:::

## Hardware

No reference answers are recorded for this revision in the registry, so its
self-check reports `unverified`; its records compare it with the package's
own runtime.
[Choose a model](model-runtime/get-started/choose-a-model.md#hardware) lists the
validated hardware.

## Quantization

The runtime loads no quantized packages of the Vela 3.0 family:
it runs at its published precision.

## Deploy it

Serve it on its own in Engine mode, to ask it directly:

<Tabs groupId="platform">
<TabItem value="cpu" label="CPU">

```bash
vllm-sr serve vllm-sr/vela3-mini --engine --platform cpu
```

Serve it on a CPU from the CPU image, as `--platform cpu` does: the ROCm
image's PyTorch has no CPU LAPACK, which this backbone needs there.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value="rocm" label="AMD GPU" default>

```bash
vllm-sr serve vllm-sr/vela3-mini --engine --platform rocm
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem value="cuda" label="NVIDIA GPU">

```bash
vllm-sr serve vllm-sr/vela3-mini --engine --platform cuda
```

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Or make it the Router's decision model:

```yaml title="config.yaml"
global:
  model_catalog:
    deployments:
      primary:
        provider: model_runtime
        artifact: vllm-sr/vela3-mini
        device: auto
    system:
      decision_model: {deployment: primary}
```

`device: auto` takes the first validated GPU with enough free memory, else
the CPU; name `rocm:0` or `cuda:0` to pin a GPU.

To run it on another host and attach the Router to it:

```bash
vllm-srun serve vllm-sr/vela3-mini --device auto --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8100
```

Then set `endpoint: http://<host>:8100` and
`model: vela3-mini` on the deployment; see
[Attach to a runtime you run](model-runtime/deploy/connect-the-router.md#attach-to-a-runtime-you-run).
